draft.why_angle: The rival pages either call the OnDash N4 a "3-Channel 4K" camera with no per-camera figure (deal.ai), give one resolution per camera at a $259.99 reference price without saying when 4K applies (my-best), or list no 3-channel camera at all (Digital Camera World's budget guide). This page gives what each under-$100 camera records with front, cabin and rear on together, from the maker's listing and manual, plus the priced GPS mount and hardwire kit.

page.title: Best 3 Channel Dash Cam Under $100 (2026 Prices, All Three Cameras On)
page.desc: Front + cabin + rear dash cams at or under $100 at their makers' US stores on 2026-11-26, compared on what each records with all three cameras on, GPS, and what parking mode adds to the price.
page.answer: Short answer. The best budget 3 channel dash cam under $100 at 2026 prices is the Vantrue OnDash N4: front, cabin and rear together record 1440P + 1080P + 1080P at 30 fps, and its 4K needs the cabin camera off. The Redtiger A3 is the lower-price pick.

page.after:
$100 is a price line dash cam shoppers search by ("3 channel dash cam under 100" and "dash cam for uber under 100" are standing search suggestions), and the third channel is the cabin camera a rideshare driver needs on top of front and rear. Every row records front, cabin and rear and was at or under $100 at its maker's US store on 2026-11-26. Left out for being just over the line: Redtiger's VP20 ($114.99) and F17 ($129.99). Cameras sold only through marketplace sellers are left out, because each row is priced at its maker's own store. Dealectric does not test units; the measurements below come from named reviewers.

The three in-stock rows are under $100 only at this week's marked-down prices: the makers' list prices are $259.99 (OnDash N4), $269.98 (A3) and $139.99 (T800E). None of the listings stated an end date. The Kingslim O3 Pro was sold out at Kingslim's store on the date read.

What the differences mean

  • What "4K" is worth with three cameras on. The N4's front camera records 2560 × 1440 = 3,686,400 pixels per frame with all three on (DashCamTalk's spec table), against 3840 × 2160 = 8,294,400 for 4K: 3,686,400 ÷ 8,294,400 = 44%.
  • Price gap. {price:vantrue-ondash-n4} − $72.74 = $27.25 more for the N4 than the Redtiger A3.
  • Parking mode. A3: $72.74 + $35.99 = $108.73. N4: {price:vantrue-ondash-n4} + $29.99 = $129.98. Neither stays under $100 once its maker's hardwire kit is added.
  • GPS. N4 with Vantrue's mount: {price:vantrue-ondash-n4} + $21.99 = $121.98. The 70mai T800E has GPS built in at $99.99.
  • Hours on a card (N4). DashCamTalk lists 15.3 + 8.3 + 6.7 = 30.3 Mb/s across front, rear and cabin (2020 review). 30.3 ÷ 8 × 3,600 = 13,635 MB, about 13.6 GB per hour. 256 ÷ 13.6 = 18.8 hours on its 256 GB maximum; 64 ÷ 13.6 = 4.7 hours on a 64 GB card. An 8-hour shift writes 8 × 13.6 = 109 GB, so it needs a 128 GB card.
  • Frame rate. The N4's three-camera mode runs at 30 fps and 70mai gives 24 fps for the T800E's 4K front: 30 ÷ 24 = 1.25 times the frames each second.

What each camera records with all three cameras on

A 3-channel camera encodes three video streams at once, so the resolution on the box is often the front camera working alone. Vantrue's own listing shows it: the headline reads "Single Front 4K | 3 Channel 4K", and the text below gives "1440P+1080P+1080P at 30fps" for front, cabin and rear together and "Single Front 4K (2160P@25fps)" for the front alone.

The N4 manual's menu page lists every mode:

  • Front + cabin + rear: 1440P + 1440P + 1080P, 1440P + 1080P + 1080P, 1080P + 1080P + 1080P, 1080P + 1080P + 720P or 720P + 720P + 720P, all at 30 fps.
  • Front + rear with the cabin camera off: 2160P + 1080P.
  • Front alone: 3840 × 2160.

4K never appears with the cabin camera on. Redtiger says the same of its F17 ($129.99, over the line): "Turn off the inside camera to enable 4K front and 1080P rear recording." 70mai's T800E listing says the system records front, interior and rear simultaneously and gives the front as 4K at 24 fps; that is the front camera's figure as 70mai states it. Redtiger and Kingslim give "2.5K" as a label, with no pixel dimensions or frame rate in the listing text read.

The N4 is the only row with named tests read for this page:

  • DashCamTalk (2020-09-22): day video 7/10, night video 5/10, reliability 8/10. Front "good video quality during the day and average quality at night"; rear "below average" at night; interior "very good in the day and average at night". Supercapacitor, −10 °C to 70 °C, cards up to 256 GB, and a separate hardwire kit for parking mode.
  • mybest: 4.27/5, third of eight 3-channel cameras. Low light 4.47, interior camera 3.97. "We were able to clearly record the numbers on license plates in both good and bad conditions." It measured a 100° horizontal front view against the 155° Vantrue lists, and notes there is no app.

Redtiger states a supercapacitor rated −20 °C to 70 °C for the A3.

Not recommended

The Refurbished OnDash N4 on Vantrue's store. It was $129.99 on 2026-11-26, more than the new camera on the same store that day.

Buying any of these for 4K with three cameras recording. On the N4, 4K needs the cabin camera off, and none of the four makers states a 4K front for a mode with the cabin camera on. If front detail matters more than the cabin view, a 2-channel camera uses the same budget better.
